summary: Describes ACTN, a framework for abstracting and controlling traffic-engineered networks. It builds on the separation of data and control planes and the many management protocols, so that customers and controllers can see and drive virtual, abstracted views of underlying networks.

eli5.summary: A big road system is complicated, so you give each user a simple map and a remote control for just the part they need.

questions: abstraction and control of te networks framework
what are cnc and pnc in actn
what is a virtual network service
subtitle: A framework for presenting customers with virtual, abstracted views of traffic-engineered networks, built from controllers at three levels.

tldr.problem: Operators of traffic-engineered networks need to give each customer its own view and control of a network, while coordinating several independent domains, technology layers and vendors underneath.
tldr.mechanism: ACTN defines a three-tier model with three controller types: the Customer Network Controller, the Multi-Domain Service Coordinator and the Provisioning Network Controller, joined by the CMI and MPI interfaces, plus rules for abstracting topology.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8453 is an Informational architecture. It does not define protocols; it provides the framework and terminology for ACTN documents and implementations.

today: RFC 8453 is an Informational document from August 2018, and the metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it. It remains the framework text for ACTN as published.

sections.title: What ACTN Is For
sections.content:
A Traffic Engineered (TE) network is one that uses any connection-oriented technology under a distributed or centralized control plane to support dynamic provisioning of end-to-end connectivity. Optical, MPLS-TP and MPLS-TE networks are examples. The RFC links the idea to Software-Defined Networking and to the Path Computation Element (RFC 4655), which can act as a logically centralized path computation function.

ACTN, Abstraction and Control of TE Networks, is a set of management and control functions used to operate one or more TE networks and build virtual networks from abstractions of them. A link in the customer's network could be built from a path or collection of paths in the underlying networks.

The framework aims to support abstraction, virtualization, TE network slicing, viewing multi-domain networks as one abstract network, and presenting customers with virtual networks over open and programmable interfaces.
sections.eli5: ACTN lets a company hand a customer a made-up simple network that is secretly built from pieces of the real one.

sections.title: Virtual Networks and Their Roles
sections.content:
A Virtual Network (VN) is a network a service provider offers a customer to use as if it were physical. A Type 1 VN is a set of edge-to-edge links, each formed as a tunnel across the underlying networks. A Type 2 VN is a topology of virtual nodes and links, and Type 1 is a special case of Type 2.

The service agreement is a Virtual Network Service (VNS). With Type 1 VNS the customer creates and operates a Type 1 VN. In Type 2a the VN is created statically and the customer cannot change its topology, while Type 2b lets the customer make dynamic changes. An Access Point (AP) is a logical identifier shared by customer and operator for an access link, and a VN Access Point (VNAP) binds an AP to a given VN.

The model has three tiers: customers, service providers and network operators. Customers range from basic ones (residential users, small enterprises) to advanced ones (enterprises and governments); the primary focus of ACTN is advanced customers. A service provider may or may not own network resources.
sections.eli5: There are the people who want a network, the company that sells it to them, and the companies that own the real cables. A customer can get a fixed map or one they can rearrange.

sections.title: Controllers and Interfaces
sections.content:
The base architecture has three controller types:

  • CNC (Customer Network Controller) communicates a customer's VNS requirements to the operator.
  • MDSC (Multi-Domain Service Coordinator) sits at the center. It does multi-domain coordination, abstraction, customer mapping and translation, and virtual service coordination.
  • PNC (Provisioning Network Controller) configures the network elements, monitors topology and collects topology information for its domain.

The interfaces are the CMI (CNC to MDSC), a business boundary between customer and operator, and the MPI (MDSC to PNC), which carries requests for new connectivity or bandwidth changes and presents an abstracted topology. The Southbound Interface (SBI) below the PNC is out of scope of ACTN. The architecture is functional, so an implementation may collocate components.

MDSCs can form a hierarchy, with a higher-level MDSC-H and lower-level MDSC-L joined by a recursion of the MPI. The MDSC functions can also be split into a service orchestrator and a network orchestrator, consistent with the YANG service model architecture of RFC 8309. A 1:N relationship between MDSCs and PNCs must be allowed.
sections.eli5: One helper talks to the customer, one boss coordinates everything, and one local worker per region does the real setup. They talk through two defined doors.

sections.title: Topology Abstraction
sections.content:
Abstraction is performed by the PNC when presenting topology to the MDSC, or by an MDSC-L when presenting to an MDSC-H. It follows the policy of the networks, and factors include the underlying technology, the capability of the PNC, scalability, and the need to keep internal details confidential. The abstraction concept comes from RFC 7926.

The RFC defines three types of abstract topology:

  • Native (white): the actual topology with no hiding.
  • Black: a whole domain becomes a single abstract node, which may impose a heavy coordination load on the MDSC with many domains.
  • Grey: a compromise exposing the border nodes. In type A they are joined by a full mesh of TE links, and in type B by a more detailed network of abstract nodes and links.

Grey topology can be built by configuration, or supplemented on demand when the MDSC sends path computation requests to PNCs, then merges the answers to pick the best end-to-end path.
sections.eli5: You can show someone the whole map, a single dot that says only that you can get in and out, or just the main junctions and how they connect.

sections.title: Multi-Destination Service
sections.content: As an advanced application, the RFC describes data center selection based on network status, called a multi-destination service. A CNC requests a VNS between a set of source and destination APs and leaves the choice of endpoints to the MDSC, in coordination with the PNCs. The MDSC chooses the best destination AP based on constraints, optimization criteria and policies, then sets up the connectivity. The candidate list is decided by the CNC or an entity outside ACTN, and later orchestration actions are outside the scope of ACTN.
sections.eli5: You say you want to reach any one of three warehouses. The network helper checks which road is clear and sets up the trip to the best one.

sections.title: Management and Security
sections.content:
ACTN manages TE resources only. OAM tasks beyond traffic engineering are not discussed. Management covers external and internal ACTN protocols, monitoring of ACTN components and policy configuration across the system.

The RFC says securing requests and control of resources, confidentiality and availability should be critical considerations. Implementations should consider encrypting data between components. Components can be a single point of failure and a threat vector. For the CMI, each CNC needs authentication and authorization, and rogue CNCs and policy conflicts must be considered. For the MPI, a PKI-based mechanism such as TLS or HTTPS is suggested between the MDSC and PNCs. Details are left to use-case-specific documents. There are no IANA actions.
sections.eli5: Because many controllers talk to each other, they need to check who is who and keep their messages private, like using locked mailboxes.
